literal: To those who withhold, where will hide, I wonder? Of those who beg, when speaking, departs life.
translation: The life of those who beg departs the moment they utter their request. Where, I wonder, will the life of those who withhold their wealth hide?
modern: இரப்பவர்கள் தம் தேவையைச் சொல்லும்போதே நாணத்தால் அவர்கள் உயிர் போய்விடுகிறது. அப்படியிருக்க, பொருளைத் தர மறுத்து மறைப்பவர்களின் உயிர் எங்கே சென்று ஒளிந்துகொள்ளுமோ?
explanation: This couplet contrasts the deep shame of the beggar with the callousness of the miser. When a person is forced to beg, the sheer humiliation of uttering the request causes their life or spirit to drain away. The poet then wonders where the life of the miser will hide when they selfishly withhold their wealth. If merely asking for help is enough to destroy a person's spirit, the act of denying that help must be an even greater burden on the soul.
